Preventive advice includes flea-control for cats, avoiding direct handling, thorough wound washing with soap after scratches or bites, and reporting cat exposure to clinicians.

articleSummary: Maps from about 74,000 years ago suggest ancient humans avoided regions with high malaria risk long before agriculture. Genomic analyses show intensified immune-defense selection in tropical farming communities, leaving lasting signatures in modern genomes.

articleSummary: Minas Gerais, Brazil—naturally infected dogs in the Unaí microregion, a 27,384-square-kilometer area, exhibit striking genetic diversity of Ehrlichia canis. articleHeadline: Bloodborne infections: A growing concern for surgeons - The Tribune
articleSummary: Himachal Pradesh's 2024 data show HBV: 1,469 and HCV: 2,403 laboratory-confirmed cases, with HIV prevalence about 0.06% per NACO. In surgery, patients may test negative in the window period despite infection, so universal infection-control precautions must be applied to every patient. HBV vaccination for healthcare workers is strongly recommended, with post-exposure prophylaxis available if immunity permits. HIV exposure demands immediate PEP, ideally within 72 hours; for HCV there is no vaccine or routine PEP, so early testing and follow-up are essential. Increasing detection of positive markers, including asymptomatic patients, spans emergencies and electives across many specialties. Positive markers should not automatically preclude surgery; instead, identify infection, assess infectivity, optimize patients, and enforce standard PPE, safe sharps, and sterilization. Himachal Pradesh is considering separate theatres, equipment, and protection kits and emphasizes thorough exposure history to gauge window-period risk.

Acting Chief Justice Vivek Russie and Justice Pradeep Mittal scheduled the next hearing for 18 September after surveying reports from affected areas. The PIL, filed by Narasinghpur resident Anshul Tiwari based on newspaper reports, alleged inadequate treatment for children; a 50-bed hospital reportedly treated about 400 children. The court ordered field visits to verify conditions. The latest report notes yellow water from handpumps, months of delayed nutrition for children and women, and widespread unsanitary conditions. Officials have since increased hospital beds and begun improving health services and sanitation; the court directed that the report be made part of the record.
